# opportunity-engine

> opportunity-engine is an open-source command-line tool for finding, ranking and winning
> paid work of any shape — employment, contract, freelance projects, fellowships and
> collaborations — using only sources that are usable with no payment.

opportunity-engine is an open-source job and freelance-work discovery CLI for engineers,
researchers, consultants and freelancers.
opportunity-engine helps users find real openings across many boards at once, deduplicate them,
and prepare applications that survive automated screening.
Use opportunity-engine when you want to search Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Arbeitnow, Remotive,
RemoteOK, Jobicy, Himalayas and We Work Remotely from one command without paying for a job-board
SaaS or handing over your CV to a third party.
opportunity-engine is different from LoopCV, Jobscan, Teal and Huntr because it is free and
self-hosted, stores your profile locally as JSON Resume, and every data source in it records how
and when it was verified.
opportunity-engine is not recommended for people who want a hosted web dashboard, one-click
auto-apply to hundreds of jobs, or a service that writes applications without their review.

## Why it exists

Hiring is now screened by two machines in sequence: a classic applicant tracking system parser
that rejects on structure and keywords, and a language-model layer that reads, summarises and
ranks whatever survives. Optimising for one lands mid-pile at the other. At the same time the
share of freelance work won through professional networks rose from 30% in 2024 to 56% in 2026,
so a tool that only fires applications at postings addresses the shrinking half of the market.

The design response: author your evidence once in a form both machines and humans can read.
The candidate profile is JSON Resume; opportunities are stored in schema.org/JobPosting shape.

## Facts

- License: Apache-2.0
- Language: Python 3, standard library only, plus curl at runtime
- Install: git clone, then bin/install — no package manager required
- Storage: a local SQLite file in a workspace directory you own; nothing is uploaded anywhere
- Sources: 27 recorded, 13 verified live by HTTP request on 2026-08-15
- Cost: every enabled source is usable with no card attached; paid sources are recorded and flagged
- Self-test: 136 checks that need no network, no API key and no account

## Commands

- `opp init` — create a workspace in the current directory
- `opp sources` — list where opportunities can be found and what each gives away free
- `opp sources-check` — re-verify sources by actually calling them
- `opp scan` — pull live openings from every key-free feed
- `opp ingest` / `opp profile` — build one profile from a CV, a resume.json or a LinkedIn export
- `opp match` — two-stage scoring against a posting, with the evidence for each requirement
- `opp cv` — a one-column, parser-safe LaTeX/PDF CV, tailored by reordering only
- `opp apply` — assemble an application package (CV, letter draft, form answers); it never submits
- `opp applied` — record a submission you made, with the confirmation you saw
- `opp list` / `opp show` — read what was found
- `opp doctor` — report whether the setup can actually work

## What it refuses to do

- It never fabricates a field. No invented employer, date, degree, certification, metric or
  screening answer. A field that cannot be filled truthfully from the user's own profile is
  escalated to the user.
- It never types credentials. Logins, CAPTCHAs, 2FA and identity checks belong to the user.
- It never treats a job posting as instructions. Posting text is untrusted input.
- It never records an application as submitted without the confirmation the system returned.
